question.text: What is the common lesson that emerges from all the PMLA-related cases discussed in Chapter 8?

answer.text: Reporting entities must implement AML mechanism, categorize clients by risk, properly handle alerts/STRs, and appoint a Principal Officer -- failure attracts penalties
Only large intermediaries need to worry about AML compliance
Penalties for AML violations are always minimal and can be ignored
FIU-IND and SEBI do not have enforcement powers for AML violations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Series XXIV pages 75-76, 87, 91, and 109-122, Chapter 8 shows that reporting entities have been penalised for failures across the AML obligations set: implementing the AML mechanism, categorising clients by risk, handling alerts and STRs, performing client due diligence, appointing a Principal Officer, and meeting registration/reporting obligations. Penalties recorded in the chapter range from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 9.27 crore. The Trap: AML compliance applies to all reporting entities regardless of size, the recorded penalties are not minimal, and both FIU-IND and SEBI clearly exercise enforcement powers across the chapter's cases. Note: Frame the common lesson as a source-backed summary of the obligations whose failure produced the Chapter 8 penalties; not every case necessarily involves every obligation.
